newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl ally names possible future chancellors.
newsitem.headline: Kohl ally names possible future chancellors.

text.p: The parliamentary leader of Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, who earlier this month mentioned himself as a possible successor to the chancellor, broadened the field on Sunday by naming eight more possible contenders.

Wolfgang Schaeuble, the wheelchair-bound politician regarded by the German media as Kohl's crown prince, named five ministers, two state premiers and one former minister as potential candidates for the chancellorship.
Kohl, 66, has consistently refused to say whether he will run again in general elections due late next year.

Schaeuble prompted a flurry of speculation about Kohl's future 11 days ago when he ended years of discretion about the succession issue and hinted in a magazine interview he would like a crack at the top job one day.

In his latest interview, however, Schaeuble insisted there were many other potential candidates, singling out the following members of the ruling coalition as those who "had what it takes for higher leadership roles":
- Kurt Biedenkopf, premier of Saxony state.
- Education and Research Minister Juergen Ruettgers.
Most of Kohl's political allies, including Schaeuble, have said they hope and expect he will stand for another term.

Some newspapers have speculated, however, that the European Union's longest-serving leader may want to bow out in 1998 or go even sooner to make way for a "grand coalition" with Germany's main opposition party, the Social Democrats.

Schaeuble, paralysed from the chest down by a would-be assassin who shot him through the spinal cord at an election rally in 1990, has said he feels capable of taking on the chancellorship despite his disabilty.
But he told Bild am Sonntag the important question was whether people would feel comfortable with a disabled chancellor.
"I don't know the answer. Experience tends to indicate not," he said. "Can you imagine someone in a wheelchair inspecting a parade?"
